gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much each triple-screen extender weighs compared with the MacBook Air it clamps onto. The Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro is 4.13 lb on a 2.7 lb 13-inch Air (1.53×) and 1.25× a 15-inch Air. The Xebec Tri-Screen 3 is 3.7 lb (1.37× and 1.12×).
standout_why: I read our own page (dealectric.com/best-triple-screen-laptop-extender-for-macbook-air), laptopbee.com's triple-screen ranking, Macworld's multi-monitor guide (675869), Macworld's best portable monitors for Mac (2836233) and Macworld's Trio 3 Pro review (3085818). None gives a MacBook Air weight or compares extender weight to laptop weight. Macworld only says the Trio 'didn't unbalance' on a laptop stand while tested on a 14-inch MacBook Pro. Our page and two ChatGPT answers compare lid width only, and only for UPERFECT (32.5 cm minimum against the 13-inch Air's 30.4 cm). No page puts the extender, laptop and combined carry weight side by side.
decides: It backs the size split ChatGPT kept giving (Trio for the 15-inch Air, Xebec for the 13-inch) with numbers. On a 13-inch Air the Trio 3 Pro hangs 4.13 lb off a 2.7 lb laptop, 53% more than the laptop weighs, and the bag weight comes to 6.83 lb. The Xebec is 37% more, for 6.4 lb in the bag, and Xebec says it fits 13–18-inch laptops. On a 15-inch Air the Trio's ratio drops to 1.25×, close to the Xebec on a 13-inch, so the Trio stays reasonable there. One more thing for the page: Macworld's review says Mobile Pixels rates the Trio for 13- to 16-inch MacBooks, but our table says 15–16 inches. Check this against mobilepixels.us before the rebuild.
